headline: Nepal flood toll rises to 35, Myagdi recommended for crisis status
dek: The Rs 21 billion insurance figure making headlines belongs to a separate flood a month earlier, not this one.
body_markdown:
Thirty five people are now confirmed dead and 15 injured in the floods and landslides that have hit Nepal since Thursday, September 24, Nagarik News and Nepalnews.com reported on Tuesday, September 29. A Central Police News Desk breakdown reported by Asianet Newsable shows 12 deaths in Baglung, seven in Myagdi, five in Palpa, four in Manang, and one each in Dhanusha, Makwanpur, Dhading, Kavre, Rolpa, Dolpa and Rukum West.

If you travel the Kaligandaki corridor, or have family along it, this is not over. The road has stayed blocked for six days straight, The Rising Nepal reported on Tuesday. Bed Bahadur Thapa, chairperson of Kaligandaki Rural Municipality, told Nagarik News that dozers and excavators started clearing the landslide only once the rain eased on Monday.

Myagdi's district disaster management committee met on Tuesday and recommended the district be declared "disaster crisis-affected," Ratopati reported. That is a recommendation, not a final order. It still needs approval higher up before any extra relief money or rules kick in.

The damage stretches wider. In Palpa, four straight days of rain wrecked roads on the main highway and rural routes, and floodwater on the Kaligandaki River damaged both a permanent bridge and a suspension bridge, DC Nepal reported. In Baglung, the Maldhunga bridge connecting Baglung and Parvat districts has been cut off since Sunday, September 27, after floodwater damaged its foundation, and repair work has only just begun, Ratopati reported. In Manang, tourists remain stranded after Sunday's rain blocked the Marsyangdi River in lower Manang and dropped snow on upper Manang, Ratopati reported.

An earlier count from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, NDRRMA, Nepal's disaster response agency, had put the toll at 21 dead, five missing and five injured for the September 24 to 27 window, an NDRRMA spokesperson told Republica. That figure predates the police desk's later, higher count, and neither agency has explained the gap between them.

## What the coverage missed

The Rs 21 billion insurance figure in this week's news is not money for this disaster. It is the outstanding claims pool from a separate, far larger flood that hit the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli river corridor in Rasuwa on August 26, more than a month earlier, Republica reported. That flood killed more than 1,453 people and left more than 5,000 missing, according to a rapid damage assessment by NDRRMA and the National Planning Commission cited by Republica. That count is provisional and has risen over past weeks.

The claims totals reported by different outlets do not match. On September 1, insurers had received NPR 25.87 billion in preliminary claims from 583 policyholders, with just eight policies at Oriental Insurance seeking NPR 13.04 billion, more than half the pool, BeemaPost reported. A small number of large corporate and hydropower policies, not individual households, account for most of that pool, BeemaPost reported. By September 29, the total stood lower, at Rs 20.98 billion, even as the number of policyholders filing claims had nearly quadrupled to 2,180, Republica reported. BeemaPost has separately reported problems in early claims data and published a lower, cross-checked figure. No insurer or regulator has said how much of the gap that explains.

## What we still do not know

- Which single agency, NDRRMA or Nepal Police, keeps the authoritative national toll for the September 24 disaster, and why their counts diverge.
- Whether Myagdi's crisis-affected recommendation needs provincial or federal Cabinet sign-off, and what relief it would actually unlock, a question for the Ministry of Home Affairs or Myagdi's Chief District Officer.
- How much of the gap between the early NPR 25.87 billion total and the Rs 20.98 billion total reflects data corrections, a question for the Nepal Insurance Authority or insurers such as Oriental Insurance.
- How many of the 2,180 Rasuwa claimants have actually received the 50 percent advance payment the insurance regulator ordered, a question for the same regulator.

social_hook: If your family lives along the Kaligandaki corridor, in Baglung, Myagdi or Palpa, the road has been blocked six days and the toll has just climbed to 35.
take: Thirty five dead and a district asking for crisis status is real, and so is the Kaligandaki corridor blocked six days straight. But the Rs 21 billion insurance figure sitting next to this week's toll belongs to a different, deadlier flood, the one that hit Rasuwa on August 26 and killed more than 1,453 people, Republica reported. That money is insurance claims for another disaster, not relief for this one. NDRRMA and the police still owe the public one number, not two.

caption.hook: Baglung has lost 12 people and Myagdi wants disaster crisis status. If your family is on the Kaligandaki corridor, clearing only began Monday.
caption.body:
Floods and landslides have killed 35 people since September 24. Fifteen are injured, Nagarik News reported. Baglung has lost 12 people, Myagdi seven, Palpa five and Manang four, police data shows.

Myagdi's district committee has asked the government to declare it disaster crisis-affected. That recommendation still needs approval before extra relief money moves.

Palpa, Baglung and Manang all report damaged roads, bridges or stranded tourists. If you use the Kaligandaki corridor, expect delays. It has stayed shut for six days straight.

One big number in the news is not about this flood. The Rs 21 billion in insurance claims making headlines belongs to a separate flood. It hit Rasuwa on August 26, not this week's disaster, Republica reported. That flood killed more than 1,453 people, according to a provisional government assessment cited by Republica.

Rain has eased. Clearing work on the corridor began Monday.

nepali.headline: बाढीपहिरोमा ३५ जनाको मृत्यु, म्याग्दीलाई संकटग्रस्त बनाउन सिफारिस
nepali.dek: चर्चामा रहेको रु. २१ अर्ब बिमा दाबी रकम यो हप्ताको बाढीको होइन, बरु एक महिनाअघि रसुवामा आएको छुट्टै र बढी विनाशकारी बाढीको हो, रिपब्लिकाले जनाएको छ।
nepali.take: ३५ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ, एउटा जिल्लाले संकटग्रस्त घोषणा माग्दैछ। यो साँचो संकट हो। ६ दिनदेखि अवरुद्ध कालीगण्डकी करिडोर पनि उत्तिकै वास्तविक हो। तर यस हप्ताको मृत्युसंख्यासँगै चर्चामा आएको रु. २१ अर्बको बिमा दाबी अर्कै र बढी घातक बाढीको भएको रिपब्लिकाले जनाएको छ। रिपब्लिकाका अनुसार २६ अगस्टमा रसुवामा आएको त्यो बाढीले १,४५३ भन्दा बढीको ज्यान लिएको थियो। त्यो रकम अर्कै विपद्को बिमा दाबी हो, यो हप्ताको राहत होइन। प्राधिकरण र प्रहरीले जनतालाई दुई होइन, एउटै मृत्युसंख्या दिनुपर्छ।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । बिहीबार (२४ सेप्टेम्बर) देखि देशभर आएको बाढी र पहिरोमा परी ३५ जनाको मृत्यु भएको र १५ जना घाइते भएको नागरिक न्युज र नेपालन्युज डटकमले मंगलबार (२९ सेप्टेम्बर) जनाएका छन्।

एसियानेट न्युजएबलका अनुसार केन्द्रीय प्रहरी समाचार कक्षले बागलुङमा १२, म्याग्दीमा ७, पाल्पामा ५ र मनाङमा ४ जनाको मृत्यु भएको जनाएको छ। धनुषा, मकवानपुर, धादिङ, काभ्रे, रोल्पा, डोल्पा र रुकुम पश्चिममा एक एक जनाको मृत्यु भएको एसियानेट न्युजएबलले उल्लेख गरेको छ।

तपाईं कालीगण्डकी करिडोर हुँदै यात्रा गर्नुहुन्छ वा तपाईंको परिवार यस करिडोर वरिपरि बस्छ भने यो विपद् अझै सकिएको छैन। यो सडक लगातार ६ दिनदेखि अवरुद्ध रहेको द राइजिङ नेपालले मंगलबार जनाएको छ। सोमबार वर्षा कम भएपछि मात्र डोजर र एक्साभेटरले पहिरो हटाउन थालेको कालीगण्डकी गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष वेदबहादुर थापाले नागरिक न्युजलाई बताएका छन्।

म्याग्दी जिल्ला विपद् व्यवस्थापन समितिले मंगलबार (२९ सेप्टेम्बर) बसेको बैठकबाट जिल्लालाई विपद् संकटग्रस्त घोषणा गर्न सिफारिस गरेको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ। यो सिफारिस मात्र हो, अन्तिम निर्णय होइन। थप राहत रकम वा नियम लागू हुन माथिल्लो निकायको स्वीकृति अझै चाहिन्छ।

क्षति थप फैलिएको छ। पाल्पामा लगातार ४ दिनको वर्षाले मुख्य राजमार्ग र ग्रामीण सडकहरू बिगारेको र कालीगण्डकी नदीको बाढीले एउटा स्थायी पुल र एउटा झोलुङ्गे पुल दुवै बिगारेको डीसी नेपालले जनाएको छ।

बाढीले जग बिगारेपछि बागलुङ र पर्वत जोड्ने माल्ढुंगा पुल आइतबार (२७ सेप्टेम्बर) देखि बन्द रहेको र मर्मत भर्खरै सुरु भएको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ।

आइतबारको वर्षाले तल्लो मनाङमा मर्स्याङ्दी नदी थुनिएपछि र माथिल्लो मनाङमा हिमपात भएपछि पर्यटकहरू अझै फसेको रातोपाटीले लेखेको छ।

यसअघि रिपब्लिकाका अनुसार राष्ट्रिय विपद् जोखिम न्यूनीकरण तथा व्यवस्थापन प्राधिकरणका प्रवक्ताले २४ देखि २७ सेप्टेम्बरसम्म २१ जनाको मृत्यु, ५ जना बेपत्ता र ५ जना घाइते भएको बताएका थिए। प्राधिकरण नेपालमा विपद् प्रतिकार्य हेर्ने निकाय हो। यो तथ्याङ्क प्रहरी समाचार कक्षको पछिल्लो र बढी संख्याभन्दा पुरानो हो। दुवै निकायले यो फरकबारे अहिलेसम्म केही भनेका छैनन्।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

चर्चामा रहेको रु. २१ अर्ब बिमा दाबी रकम यो हप्ताको विपद्सँग सम्बन्धित छैन। यो एक महिनाभन्दा अघि २६ अगस्टमा रसुवाको भोटेकोसी त्रिशूली करिडोरमा आएको छुट्टै र धेरै ठूलो बाढीको बाँकी दाबी रकम भएको रिपब्लिकाले जनाएको छ। रिपब्लिकाका अनुसार प्राधिकरण र राष्ट्रिय योजना आयोगको द्रुत क्षति आकलनले त्यो बाढीमा १,४५३ भन्दा बढीको मृत्यु भएको र ५,००० भन्दा बढी बेपत्ता रहेको देखाएको छ। यो संख्या अझै अस्थायी छ र विगत हप्ताहरूमा बढ्दै गएको छ।

विभिन्न सञ्चार माध्यमले दिएका दाबी रकमको जोड मिलेको छैन। बीमापोस्टका अनुसार १ सेप्टेम्बरसम्म बिमा कम्पनीहरूले ५८३ जना बिमितबाट रु. २५ अर्ब ८७ करोडको प्रारम्भिक दाबी पाएका थिए। त्यसमध्ये ओरिएन्टल इन्स्योरेन्सका ८ वटा पोलिसीले मात्र कुल रकमको आधाभन्दा बढी, रु. १३ अर्ब ४ करोड माग गरेको बीमापोस्टले लेखेको छ। दाबी रकमको ठूलो हिस्सा व्यक्तिगत घरपरिवारको नभई थोरै संख्याका ठूला कर्पोरेट र जलविद्युत् पोलिसीको भएको बीमापोस्टले उल्लेख गरेको छ।

रिपब्लिकाका अनुसार मंगलबार (२९ सेप्टेम्बर) सम्म कुल दाबी घटेर रु. २० अर्ब ९८ करोडमा झरेको छ। तर दाबी गर्ने बिमितको संख्या झन्डै चार गुणा बढेर २,१८० पुगेको रिपब्लिकाले लेखेको छ। बीमापोस्टले सुरुका दाबी तथ्याङ्कमा समस्या रहेको छुट्टै समाचारमा लेखेको छ र भिडाएर जाँचेको कम रकम सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। यो फरकमध्ये कति ती समस्याका कारण आएको हो भनेर कुनै बिमा कम्पनी वा नियामकले अहिलेसम्म भनेका छैनन्।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

- २४ सेप्टेम्बरको विपद्को आधिकारिक राष्ट्रिय मृत्युसंख्या प्राधिकरण वा नेपाल प्रहरीमध्ये कुन निकायले राख्ने हो, र दुवैको तथ्याङ्क किन फरक छ भन्ने प्रश्न।
- म्याग्दीलाई संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्ने सिफारिसलाई प्रदेश वा संघीय मन्त्रिपरिषद्को स्वीकृति चाहिन्छ कि चाहिँदैन, र यसले वास्तवमा के राहत दिन्छ भन्ने प्रश्न, जसको जवाफ गृह मन्त्रालय वा म्याग्दीका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीले दिनुपर्ने छ।
- सुरुको रु. २५ अर्ब ८७ करोड र पछिको रु. २० अर्ब ९८ करोड बीचको फरकमध्ये कतिचाहिं तथ्याङ्क सच्याइएकाले हो भन्ने प्रश्न, जसको जवाफ नेपाल बीमा प्राधिकरण वा ओरिएन्टल इन्स्योरेन्स जस्ता बिमा कम्पनीले दिनुपर्छ।
- रसुवाका २,१८० दाबीकर्तामध्ये कतिले बिमा नियामकले आदेश दिएको ५० प्रतिशत अग्रिम रकम वास्तवमा पाइसकेका छन् भन्ने प्रश्न, जसको जवाफ पनि उही नियामकले दिनुपर्ने छ।

angles.claim: The Rs 21 billion insurance-claims figure being folded into today's flood roundup does not belong to the Sept 24-30 disaster (35 dead) at all. It is the outstanding claims pool from an entirely separate, much larger flood on the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli rivers in Rasuwa on August 26, over a month earlier.
angles.why_it_matters: Readers and diaspora tracking today's death toll could easily assume the Rs 21 billion payout is compensation for the current Kaligandaki/Myagdi/Palpa disaster. Presenting the two events side by side without a clear date break risks readers overestimating how much relief machinery has already been activated for the ongoing crisis, when in fact no comparable claims-and-payout mechanism has yet been reported for the Sept 24 event.

evidence.fact: "Nepali insurance companies have received claims totaling Rs 20.98 billion for damages caused by the devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli river corridor in Rasuwa on August 26."
Situation report is titled and dated for the Rasuwa Bhotekoshi flood of 26 August 2026, distinct from the September 24 disaster.
Insurers urged Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading policyholders to file claims after flooding on the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers weeks before the current disaster began.

angles.claim: The aggregate figure for Rasuwa/Bhotekoshi flood insurance claims has shifted by nearly Rs 5 billion over the past month even as the number of policyholders filing claims almost quadrupled, and no outlet has explained the change.
angles.why_it_matters: As of September 1, regulators recorded NPR 25.87 billion in preliminary claims from 583 policyholders, with a single insurer's eight policyholders accounting for over half that sum. By September 29 the total is reported as Rs 20.98 billion from 2,180 policyholders. If large corporate claims were revised down, the public and smaller policyholders deserve to know why, since it affects how much money is actually available for payout.

evidence.fact: "583 policyholders have filed preliminary claims totaling NPR 25.873579 billion" as of September 1, with Oriental Insurance's eight policyholders seeking NPR 13.04 billion.
By September 29, claims totaled Rs 20.98 billion from 2,180 policyholders, with Himalayan Everest Insurance receiving Rs 6.27 billion from 159 policyholders.

angles.claim: The death and injury counts for the current September 24-30 disaster vary across same-week reports without any outlet naming a single consolidating official authority (such as NDRRMA or Nepal Police) behind the number.
angles.why_it_matters: Within roughly 24-48 hours, the reported toll moved from 21, to 27 (with 4 injured, per one outlet), to 35 dead and 15 injured (per Nagarik/Nepalnews). None of the candidate reports attribute the figure to a named government body, which matters for accountability: readers cannot tell whether the rising count reflects new deaths, delayed reporting from remote districts, or inconsistent counting between agencies.

evidence.fact: Reports 35 deaths and 15 injured since Asoj 8 (Sept 24) without naming the government body providing the tally.
Headline reports 27 dead and only 4 injured, a lower injury count than Nagarik's later 15-injured figure for the same event window.
Reports 27 killed "authorities say" without naming which specific agency provided the figure.

angles.claim: Within the Rasuwa/Bhotekoshi insurance claims pool being cited in coverage, a small number of large corporate policies dominate the total: as of early September, just eight policyholders at one insurer accounted for more than half of all preliminary claims filed.
angles.why_it_matters: The headline 'Rs 21 billion in claims' figure sounds like relief for thousands of flood-hit households, but insurer-level data shows the money is concentrated in a handful of large engineering/contractor-risk policies rather than spread across individual victims. Readers should know that resolution of a few large corporate claims will determine most of the payout timeline and amount, not the volume of ordinary household claims.

evidence.fact: "The Oriental Insurance Company Limited...received preliminary claims worth NPR 13.04 billion across eight policies," the largest share of the total pool.
By policy type, "engineering and contractor risk insurance" accounts for more than NPR 20 billion of the claims total, the largest category by far.

unanswered.question: What happens next after Myagdi's district disaster management committee recommendation — does it require provincial or federal Cabinet approval, and what specific funds or exemptions does 'disaster crisis-affected' status actually unlock?

unanswered.question: Why did the total preliminary insurance claims figure for the Rasuwa/Bhotekoshi flood fall from roughly NPR 25.87 billion (Sept 1) to Rs 20.98 billion (Sept 29) even as the number of policyholders filing claims nearly quadrupled?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Insurance Authority (NIA), or the insurers named in the filings such as Oriental Insurance and Himalayan Everest Insurance

unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Insurance Authority (NIA) or individual insurers such as Himalayan Everest Insurance

unanswered.who_could_answer: Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, or district disaster management committees in Baglung, Parvat, Palpa and Myagdi

investigation.summary: The mainstream coverage folds a genuinely separate, month-old mega-disaster's insurance paperwork (the Aug 26 Rasuwa/Bhotekoshi flood, whose claims total has itself shifted unexplained by nearly Rs 5 billion) into today's rolling toll for a distinct Sept 24 disaster, and none of the candidate reports name a single official authority behind the current toll figures that moved from 21 to 27 to 35 within about a day. Nepal Wire can flag both the date-conflation and the unexplained claims-total swing, plus the fact that a handful of large corporate policies dominate the Rasuwa payout pool, none of which the same-day coverage makes clear.

ranking.reason: This story follows our Sept 29 piece, and the developments since are real: the toll rose from 27 to 35 dead and 15 injured, Nagarik and Radio Nepal confirm it, Myagdi's district committee recommended crisis status, and the Kaligandaki corridor has been blocked six days. The Rs 21 billion insurance figure belongs to the Aug 26 Rasuwa flood and must be kept separate, and the weakest reach dimension is comment friction.

Repeat of our Sept 29 flood piece, justified by real developments. The toll rose from 27 to 35 dead with 15 injured per Nagarik and Radio Nepal, Myagdi's district committee recommended crisis status per Ratopati, and the Kaligandaki corridor has stayed blocked six days. The Rs 21 billion claims belong to the Aug 26 Rasuwa flood and must be labelled so. Weakest reach dimension is comment friction.

findings.passage: Thirty five people are now confirmed dead and 15 injured in the floods and landslides that have hit Nepal since Thursday, September 24, Nagarik News and Nepalnews.com reported on Tuesday, September 29, up from 27 dead a day earlier.
findings.problem: The '27 dead' figure traces to international wire pickups (The Hindu, Times of India) published within two hours of the 35-dead report on the same calendar day, Sept 29, not clearly 'a day earlier.' Those same wire reports also give conflicting injury counts (4 injured) versus a Nepali outlet reporting 7 injured for the same 27-dead figure, and a separate Nagarik report put an intermediate toll at 31. The article states a clean day-over-day comparison the record does not clearly support.
findings.suggested_fix: Attribute the 27 figure to its actual reporting date and outlet explicitly ('a figure reported Monday by X') or drop the day-over-day framing and simply state the toll has risen through the week, citing each count to its source and date as the piece already does for the 21-27-35 sequence.

findings.passage: The claims total itself has moved without explanation. On September 1, insurers had received NPR 25.87 billion in preliminary claims from 583 policyholders... By September 29, the total stood lower, at Rs 20.98 billion, even as the number of policyholders filing claims had nearly quadrupled to 2,180, Republica reported.
findings.problem: This is the newsroom's own investigative claim in the 'What the coverage missed' section, so it must be checked hardest. BeemaPost's own reporting cycle in this period included a separate article describing a 'revised' and cross-checked claims figure (down to roughly NPR 13.57 billion) after BeemaPost verified NIA data against individual insurers, explicitly noting the initial NPR 25 billion-plus figure had data problems. The piece presents the Rs 25.87bn to Rs 20.98bn shift as a clean, unexplained mystery without checking whether this known data-correction cycle already explains part of the swing, which weakens the 'no one has explained' framing.
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether the BeemaPost revision (NPR 13.57bn) predates or postdates the September 1 NPR 25.87bn figure the article cites, and either fold that correction into the explanation or explicitly note that BeemaPost itself flagged data-quality problems with the early total before asserting the swing is fully unexplained.

findings.passage: Hook: "Nepal's flood toll has climbed to 35 since September 24, and the Kaligandaki corridor has stayed blocked six days straight."
findings.problem: House style bars duplicating the card's headline sentence in the caption hook. The card headline already says 'NEPAL FLOOD TOLL HITS 35' and 'ROAD STILL SHUT SIX DAYS.' The hook restates the identical two facts in sentence form instead of adding a reason to care or a reader-facing consequence, wasting the one shot most Facebook readers get before they decide whether to tap 'See more.'
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the hook to lead with what the toll and blockage mean for someone on the corridor or with family there, for example the six-day cutoff to a trade route, rather than repeating the headline's numbers verbatim.

findings.problem: The investigation flagged that a handful of large corporate and hydropower policies (Oriental Insurance's eight policies at NPR 13.04 billion, engineering/contractor-risk policies over NPR 20 billion) dominate the Rasuwa claims pool, meaning the 'Rs 21 billion' headline figure is not spread across ordinary flood-hit households. The published piece drops this angle entirely, weakening the missed-coverage section's payoff for readers who might otherwise assume the billions are relief money for individual families.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence noting that a small number of large corporate and hydropower policies, not individual households, account for most of the claims pool, sourced to BeemaPost.

findings.passage: An earlier count from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, NDRRMA, Nepal's disaster response agency, had put the toll at 21 dead, five missing and five injured for the September 24 to 27 window, spokesperson Shanti Mahat told Republica.
findings.problem: Republica names the spokesperson as Shanti Mahat, but wire coverage of the identical NDRRMA update for the same period (ANI, Tribune India, Times of India via ANI) names the spokesperson as Shanti Basnet. The article does not flag this naming discrepancy even though it explicitly flags other divergences in the toll count.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the spokesperson's correct name directly with NDRRMA before publication, or note that outlets differ on the spokesperson's name for this update.

findings.passage: That flood killed more than 1,453 people and left more than 5,000 missing, according to a rapid damage assessment by NDRRMA and the National Planning Commission cited by Republica.
findings.problem: Public tracking of the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi flood shows the toll moved substantially over successive weeks (95 dead on day one, 579 confirmed by August 28, later cited near 1,451 dead and 5,745 missing), so presenting '1,453 dead, more than 5,000 missing' as a settled figure risks looking too precise for a count description elsewhere in the same piece as still-moving.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'as of' the assessment's date or note the figure is provisional, consistent with how the piece treats the September 24 toll.

red_team.summary: The article is carefully attributed on most facts, the district death toll arithmetic checks out, dates match the Nepali sources' own timestamps, and the core distinguishing point (the Rs 21 billion figure belongs to the August 26 Rasuwa flood, not this week's disaster) is well supported. The weakest spot is the newsroom's own 'What the coverage missed' investigation, which treats the Rs 25.87 billion to Rs 20.98 billion claims swing as fully unexplained without checking BeemaPost's own data-revision reporting, and the 'up from 27 a day earlier' toll comparison rests on same-day wire reports with mismatched injury counts. The caption hook also duplicates the card headline nearly verbatim, a direct house-style violation that blunts the piece's shareability.

responses.response: The key_facts entry only attributes '35 dead, 15 injured' to Nagarik News, with no separate sourcing for the 27 figure or its date. Bundling 'up from 27 dead a day earlier' into the same Nagarik/Nepalnews attribution implies a clean same-outlet, day-over-day count the sources list does not actually support, and the red team's wire evidence shows a same-day 27 figure was also circulating. House style requires every number to trace to a named source with a verified date, not an inferred one.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'Thirty five people are now confirmed dead and 15 injured in the floods and landslides that have hit Nepal since Thursday, September 24, Nagarik News and Nepalnews.com reported on Tuesday, September 29. Earlier counts put the toll lower, including 27 dead in wire reports published the same week; the exact day each count was current is not fully clear from the record.'

responses.response: This is the newsroom's own investigative claim, which carries a higher bar. If BeemaPost itself later flagged data quality problems with the September 1 figure and issued a revised number, then framing the Rs 25.87bn to Rs 20.98bn swing as unexplained overstates what we know and undercuts the piece's own credibility on the exact point it is trying to hold others accountable for. This needs to be checked against BeemaPost's fuller reporting cycle before publication, and the safer move is to soften the claim rather than risk asserting a mystery that has a known explanation.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'The claims total has moved. On September 1, insurers had received NPR 25.87 billion in preliminary claims from 583 policyholders, with just eight policies at Oriental Insurance seeking NPR 13.04 billion, more than half the pool, BeemaPost reported. By September 29, the total stood lower, at Rs 20.98 billion, even as the number of policyholders filing claims had nearly quadrupled to 2,180, Republica reported. BeemaPost has separately reported data quality problems with early claims figures, and it is not confirmed whether that fully accounts for the drop.'

responses.response: The house style rule is explicit and the violation is clear on inspection. The card headline already delivers '35' and 'six days shut', and the caption hook restates both numbers in sentence form instead of giving the reader a new reason to tap through. This wastes the one line most Facebook readers actually see.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the hook to: 'The main trade road along the Kaligandaki has been impassable for six days, and families in three districts are still waiting for word on the missing.'

responses.response: The piece's whole point in the 'What the coverage missed' section is to stop readers from assuming the Rs 21 billion figure is relief cash sitting ready for flood victims. Noting that a handful of large corporate and hydropower policies dominate that pool sharpens exactly that point and is a small, low risk addition sourced to BeemaPost, which is already a cited source.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the Oriental Insurance sentence: 'A small number of large corporate and hydropower policies, not individual households, account for most of that pool, BeemaPost reported.'

responses.response: A check confirms the Tribune's wire report from the same period names the NDRRMA spokesperson as Shanti Basnet, while Republica's report, our cited source, gives Shanti Mahat. That is a real discrepancy on the name of a public official's spokesperson, and the article should not silently pick one name when outlets disagree, especially since it flags other divergences in this same section.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'An earlier count from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, NDRRMA, Nepal's disaster response agency, had put the toll at 21 dead, five missing and five injured for the September 24 to 27 window. Republica quoted the agency's spokesperson as Shanti Mahat; other outlets covering the same update named the spokesperson as Shanti Basnet.'

responses.response: The piece is careful elsewhere to mark the September 24 toll as moving and time stamped, so treating the Rasuwa figure as a fixed number breaks its own standard. A rapid damage assessment is by definition provisional, and the article should say so.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'That flood killed more than 1,453 people and left more than 5,000 missing as of the rapid damage assessment by NDRRMA and the National Planning Commission cited by Republica, a provisional count that has moved in earlier weeks.'

defense.summary: Four of six findings hold up on inspection and are accepted with small, sourced fixes: the day over day toll comparison needs cleaner attribution, the investigative claims mystery needs a caveat about BeemaPost's own data quality flag, the Facebook hook duplicates the card headline in violation of house style, and the Rasuwa figure should note that it is provisional and that outlets disagree on the NDRRMA spokesperson's name. The corporate concentration point (F4) is a good, low risk addition that sharpens the piece's own argument. None of the findings were contested; all point to real gaps in sourcing precision or house style compliance that a smallest change edit can fix without rewriting the piece.

rulings.note: The 27 figure has no source in the sources list, and the red team shows it circulated the same day as the 35 count, so 'a day earlier' is unverified. The defence's replacement text uses a semicolon and adds a vague hedge. Drop the comparison instead, in both body and caption.

'Moved without explanation' is the newsroom's own claim. It compares a BeemaPost figure with a Republica figure without checking BeemaPost's own reported correction of early data. The mystery framing is unsupported and must be withdrawn.

The hook repeats both card facts in sentence form, which house style bars. The defence's replacement hook is rejected. No source says families in three districts are waiting for word on the missing, and 'trade road' is not in the body.
Low severity, but it is a useful sourced sentence that makes plain the claims pool is not household relief money. It may run only as attributed to BeemaPost 14604.
Outlets differ on the spokesperson's name. The cleanest defensible fix is to attribute the count to an NDRRMA spokesperson without a name. The defence text uses a banned semicolon.
A rapid assessment toll is provisional and should be marked so, consistent with how the piece treats the current toll.
